newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar to set up $400 million steel venture.
newsitem.headline: Qatar to set up $400 million steel venture.

text.p: Qatar Steel Company (QASCO) will sign a $400 million joint venture deal with a group of foreign firms in February to produce hot briquetted iron (HBI) in the Gulf Arab state, the company said on Wednesday.

Three Japanese, one European and two Kuwaiti firms will take a 49 percent stake in the company which will produce two million tonnes a year of HBI -- used in steel plants to make smolten steel -- from early 1999, QASCO general manager Nasser al-Mansouri said.
QASCO will hold 31 percent and Qatar Industrial Manufacturing Company and Qatar Shipping Company will each hold 10 percent of Qatar Hot Briquetted Iron Company (QABICO), he said.
"A memorandum of understanding was signed on December 18, 1996, and the joint venture agreement will be signed on February 12, 1997," Mansouri said in a statement.

He said the Japanese and the European partners who will equally share 40 percent of the venture's equity had agreed to buy 80 percent -- 1.6 million tonnes a year -- of QABICO's production, and the rest was to be bought by QASCO.
The shareholders are Japan's Mitsubishi Corp, Mitsui Corp and Marubeni Corp and Duferco Participations Holding Ltd, of Guernsey in the Channel Islands.

The Kuwaiti partners -- Gulf Investment Corporation and National Industries Company of Kuwait -- will each hold a 4.5 percent share of the firm and help in financing the project but will not buy the plant's production.

Qatar's Minister of Electricity and Water Ahmad Mohammad Ali al-Subai'e, who is also QASCO's chairman, said QABICO's nine partners would raise 30 percent of the project's cost through equity and 70 percent will be financed by loans arranged by a consortium of local and international banks.
The project will use Qatar's abundant natural gas to operate.
QASCO said it was also testing a new rolling mill to add 140,000 tonnes of reinforced steel bars to its 330,000 tonnes per year designed capacity.
The new mill, which forms part of the company's internal expansion programme, is expected to launch commercial production after March, the statement said.
QASCO's other expansion projects include the setting up of a 1.2 billion riyal ($329.6 million) plant to produce 500,000 tonnes a year of reinforced steel bars.
QASCO is a joint venture of the state, which holds 70 percent, Japan's Kobe Steel, which holds 20 percent, and Tokyo Boeki, which has 10 percent of the stakes.
